report:
Fixed F1 (medium) and F2 (low) in the target file only. Both fixes were checked against S33 section 6 (the T15 row, the token-expectation preamble, the T17 row, and 'Each of T01-T17 obtains r2 before any other assertion or subTest'), S33 section 7 (loading and effects), S34 tests.tokenExpectation and tests.T17, and the S45 readoption decision. No mandatory fix conflicted with these.

F1, in test_T15_detachment_nonaliasing_and_source_effects:
- _prepare() is still the first statement. Its return value is no longer used.
- The method then asserts that sys.modules['host_codec'] is FIX['host'] and snapshots the host identities. It builds a fresh module with _module('c2_issue_artifacts_r2', FIX['r2_bytes']), which execs into a new ModuleType. That uses no sys.path or import machinery, registers nothing in sys.modules and installs no proxy, so the module binds the pinned host.
- It takes prepare_c2_issue from the fresh module's __dict__, with the same FunctionType guard that _prepare uses.
- It takes the namespace keys, the identities and the deep-copied container state from that fresh module before the module's first call.
- Every T15 call goes through that fresh prepare: first, second, third (previously self.call, which used the shared FIX['r2']), and all nine T14 refusals plus CASE_CARDANO_ANCHOR (prepare=prepare).
- All earlier assertions are kept, in the same order: input deep-copy equality, no input/result container aliasing, two results sharing no container, mutating a result leaving later results unchanged, namespace keys and identities, mutable-global state, held containers versus kept inputs and results, host identities and sys.modules host, and the EFFECT_TOKENS scan.
- One change in the host check: the host snapshot is now taken before the fresh exec, so the existing 'host not patched' assertion also covers import-time effects of the fresh module.
- I extended the existing residual comment to say that caching in non-container state remains a source-inspection obligation.

F2, the module docstring:
- It now describes the whole combined Part A/B/C source with 18 methods. RED and GREEN are stated as unobserved, and it says a fresh non-author audit is required.
- It states that the only computed expectations are the S33 section 6 hashlib.blake2b(digest_size=32) NON-ORACLE token values over a literal expected envCborHex, plus the T17 SYNTHETIC_NOT_PROOF_NOT_ORACLE statement digest and x1/x2. These are independent of host_codec but not of hashlib, and are not evidence about Rust or any proof. Every other expectation is a literal, or literal framing around fixture bytes and those computed values, and none is host_codec output. v1 equality is described as shared-host consistency, not an oracle.
- The read/effect description stays accurate. It now also covers the r2 bytes being executed by _prepare, again in T01 against a counting proxy, and again in T15 against the pinned host, never registered in sys.modules. It also covers T01's temporary proxy swap and its restore, and that r2 is re-read only if its exec fails.

Untouched: all executable Part A code, Part B tables and helpers, the class helpers, T00-T14, T16, T17 and the main tail. There are still exactly 18 test methods. F3 was not applied. Because the docstring changed, the old 7864-byte Part A prefix is not preserved in the new candidate. The old frozen candidate's provenance is unaffected.

RED prediction (unobserved): unchanged. T15 still fails at its leading _prepare() with MISSING_R2 while r2 is absent.
limitations: Nothing was executed, imported, compiled or tested. I used only Read and Edit. The new byte count and SHA-256 were not computed, and root must pin them.
The changed bytes are confined to the two allowed regions by construction of the edits, but this was not byte-diffed against the old 57480-byte candidate (9b539d7d...).

The class helper call() is now unused, because T15 was its only caller. It was left in place since it is outside the allowed regions. This has no effect on the method count, because it has no test prefix.

T15 adds two guard assertions needed to bind the fresh module safely: sys.modules['host_codec'] is FIX['host'] before the exec, and the fresh prepare_c2_issue is a FunctionType, mirroring _prepare. It adds no new cases.

The fresh-module baseline detects in-place container mutation or caching that settles on first use. Caching in non-container state (function attributes, closures, object instances) is still a source-inspection obligation, as are the CP04, CP01 and I1 residuals.
F3 (filename-scoped FileNotFoundError) was deliberately not applied, per the reviewer's decision.
The new whole candidate needs a fresh non-author actual claude-opus-5-5 audit before any ROOT RED. This grants no execution, adoption, implementation or builder reliance.
